decisions.item_text: The certifying person responsible for final batch certification and the marketing authorisation holder make sure that the product quality review is completed on time and is accurate.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers the responsibility of the certifying person and the authorisation holder for a timely, accurate quality review.
Both state that the excipient risk assessment considers whether an effective quality system is in place.
Both state that the assessment considers whether there are enough competent, qualified staff.
Both state that the assessment considers job descriptions for managerial and supervisory staff.
Both state that the assessment considers training programmes for all manufacturing and quality staff; the listed areas are only examples.
Both state that the assessment considers health, hygiene and clothing training where needed.
Both state that the assessment considers suitable, maintained premises and equipment.
Both state that the assessment considers documentation systems covering all processes and specifications.
Both state that the assessment considers coding and identification of materials for full traceability.
Both state that the assessment considers a supplier qualification programme.
Both state that the assessment considers excipient quality control and an independent person releasing batches.
Both state that the assessment considers retention of incoming-material records and excipient samples for the required periods.
Both state that the assessment considers written contracts for all outsourced activities.
Both state that the assessment considers an effective complaint review and recall system.
Both state that the assessment considers a change and deviation management system.
Both state that the assessment considers environmental control and storage conditions.

decisions.item_text: The distributor of active substances carries out self-inspections and records them, to monitor that good distribution practice is put in place and followed.
decisions.reason: Existing self-inspection requirements address GMP compliance by manufacturers, not distributor self-inspections against distribution practice.
Both state that self-inspections are carried out regularly following an approved schedule.
